message: Encrypt the secrets stored in the database, with local keys or HashiCorp Vault
bullet_points: API tokens, MCP endpoint keys, 2FA secrets, integration and data sync credentials, SSO client secrets, AI provider keys, webhooks and audit log parameters are encrypted with AES-256-GCM. A leaked database dump or stolen database credentials only expose ciphertext.

The keys are held by a key provider: a key derived from SECRET_KEY by default, dedicated keys set with BASEROW_ENCRYPTION_KEYS, or a HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao Transit key with BASEROW_ENCRYPTION_PROVIDER=hashicorp_vault.

After upgrading, secrets are still written in plain text so that the previous version keeps working during a rolling upgrade. Run `./baserow encrypt_data` once every instance runs the new version: it enables encryption and encrypts the existing secrets. The `baserow/baserow` image does this automatically on startup. Run it again after every key rotation.
Changing SECRET_KEY makes the encrypted secrets unreadable when no dedicated key is configured. Configure BASEROW_ENCRYPTION_KEYS and run `./baserow encrypt_data` first.
